title: Glacier Evolution on the Hurd Peninsula, Livingston Island, Antarctica, from 1957 to 2025:  Integrating Geomatic Methods and GNSS-R  Data for Intermediate Glacier Surface Estimation
content:
This paper presents an original methodology to generate continuous Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) for glaciers at any time, moving beyond constraints of specific survey dates. Normally, these surveys take place in only in specific dates, during Antarctic campaigns. While these traditional measurements provide precise data, they are in-herently limited to specific acquisition dates. To overcome this limitation, our ap-proach estimates DEMs at any given time of the year by applying advanced interpola-tion techniques to data collected continuously via GNSS antennas and Global Naviga-tion Satellite System-Reflectometry (GNSS-R) technology. We apply this method to analyze the evolution of Johnsons and Hurd glaciers on Livingston Island, Antarctica, for a period spanning from 1957 to 2025 and we obtain a DEM for Johnsons and Hurd glaciers for Spring 2024. 
To determine bedrock topography, Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) techniques are widely utilized. Bedrock topography is estimated by subtracting the measured ice-thickness from the glacier surface elevation determined from geodetic surveys. However, GPR campaigns rarely coincide in time with geodetic surveys. Therefore, es-tablishing a time-specific surface reference is critical. Likewise, during polar summer campaigns, tracking continuously surface elevation changes is very important.
Therefore, the development of a methodology to generate DEMs for any day of the year is very important to integrate it with data obtained using GPR. The Numerical Simu-la-tion Group in Science and Engineering (GSNCI) previously produced a high-resolution DEM of the Johnsons and Hurd glaciers for 2013 and subsequently generated an updated DEM for 2025 during the 2024-2025 Spanish Antarctic Cam-paign. Using GNSS-R data, we here calculate an estimated DEM for the end of 2024.
